newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela questions electricity power losses.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela questions electricity power losses.

text.p: Venezuela's Electricity Regulatory Committee queried the levels of power losses reported by state- owned electricity companies in their requests for higher tariffs, a senior government official said on Tuesday.
The companies "lose" electricity in poor quality transmission lines, administrative inefficiency and theft through illegal connections and meter tampering.
Deputy Energy and Mines Minister Evanan Romero said Cadafe reported a 27 percent loss, Enelven-Enelco 37.42 percent and Enelbar 12 percent.
Romero said he recognised power losses of 23 percent for Cadafe, 21 percent for Enelven-Enelco and 12 percent for Enelbar.
The companies, which are the main ones slated for privatisation under a bill currently being discussed in Congress, notched up over $700 million in financial losses last year.

Mariano Crespo, general manager of the Fondo de Inversiones de Venezuela (FIV) privatisation unit, said the losses were largely due to their high levels of debt which in Cadafe's case reached $1.2 billion.

Crespo detailed the companies' 1996 results: 345 billion bolivar losses for Cadafe (equivalent to $717 million at current exchange rates); 4.1 billion bolivar ($8.5 million) losses for Enelbar; and 23 billion bolivar ($47.8 million) losses for Enelven-Enelco.
Crespo said the conditions of sale have not been drawn up yet because the new Electricity Law governing regulation has not been defined by Congress.

To avoid any further deterioration in the level of service given by these companies, Crespo said the government injected eight billion bolivars ($16.6 million) of capital into Enelven- Enelco and 5.4 billion ($11.2 million) into Enelbar.
He said Cadafe, which supplies electricity to the other two companies, needed 73.6 billion bolivars ($153 million) in investment this year.
